54697-the-baita-l-pachchisi-or-the-twent.description: A book by John Platts. The first said, ‘A man bitten by a snake on the fifth, sixth, eighth, nine, or fourteenth day of the lunar month does not survive.’ A second said, ‘One who has been bitten on a Saturday or Tuesday, too, does not live.

arxiv-1412-6407.title: Enhancing SfePy with Isogeometric Analysis
arxiv-1412-6407.creator: Robert Cimrman
arxiv-1412-6407.description: Abstract In the paper a recent enhancement to the open source package SfePy (Simple Finite Elements in Python, http://sfepy.org ) is introduced, namely the addition of another numerical discretization scheme, the isogeometric analysis, to the original implementation based on the nowadays standard and well-established numerical solution technique, the finite element method.

arxiv-2102-00022.title: MICROSCOPE’s constraint on a short-range fifth force Journal: Class. Quantum Grav.
arxiv-2102-00022.creator: Joel Bergé, Martin Pernot-Borràs, Jean-Philippe Uzan, Philippe Brax, Ratana Chhun, Gilles Métris, Manuel Rodrigues, Pierre Touboul
arxiv-2102-00022.description: Abstract The MICROSCOPE experiment was designed to test the weak equivalence principle in space, by comparing the low-frequency dynamics of cylindrical “free-falling” test masses controlled by electrostatic forces. We use data taken during technical sessions aimed at estimating the electrostatic stiffness of MICROSCOPE’s sensors to constrain a short-range Yukawa deviation from Newtonian gravity.

arxiv-2107-00940.title: Inverse-Dirichlet Weighting Enables Reliable Training of Physics Informed Neural Networks
arxiv-2107-00940.creator: Suryanarayana Maddu 1,2,3,7 , Dominik Sturm 9,10 , Christian L. Müller 4,5,6 , Ivo F. Sbalzarini 1,2,3,7,8
arxiv-2107-00940.description: Abstract We characterize and remedy a failure mode that may arise from multi-scale dynamics with scale imbalances during training of deep neural networks, such as Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). PINNs are popular machine-learning templates that allow for seamless integration of physical equation models with data.

arxiv-2201-12670.title: SMGRL: Scalable Multi-resolution Graph Representation Learning
arxiv-2201-12670.creator: Reza Namazi namazir@mcmaster.ca, Elahe Ghalebi elahe.ghalebi@vectorinstitute.ai, Sinead A. Williamson sinead@austin.utexas.edu, Hamidreza Mahyar mahyarh@mcmaster.ca
arxiv-2201-12670.description: Abstract Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) allow us to learn topologically-aware node embeddings, which can be useful for classification or link prediction. However, they are unable to capture long-range dependencies between nodes without adding additional layers—which in turn leads to over-smoothing and increased time and space complexity.

arxiv-2308-11789.title: Taylor halos and Taylor spears in odd viscous liquids
arxiv-2308-11789.creator: E. Kirkinis, M. Olvera de la Cruz
arxiv-2308-11789.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by E. Kirkinis, M. Olvera de la Cruz. A body placed in a rigidly-rotating fluid becomes circumscribed by a fictitious cylinder with generators parallel to the axis of rotation, a Taylor column. Slowly-moving liquid impinging on the body will swerve around the cylinder. Thus, Taylor columns may form when a breeze impinges on a mountain or when slowly-moving oceanic water impinges on a seamount, both due to the Earth’s rotation.

arxiv-2308-15604.title: On a dynamical system linked to the BKL scenario
arxiv-2308-15604.creator: Robert Conte
arxiv-2308-15604.description: Abstract We consider the six-dimensional dynamical system in three components introduced by Ryan to describe the scenario of Belinskii, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz to the cosmological singularity when the spatial metric tensor is not diagonal. Despite its nonintegrability, recently proven by Goldstein and Piechocki, the three four-dimensional systems defined by canceling one of the three components happen to be integrable.

arxiv-2309-16569.title: Audio-Visual Speaker Verification via Joint Cross-Attention
arxiv-2309-16569.creator: R. Gnana Praveen, Jahangir Alam
arxiv-2309-16569.description: Abstract Speaker verification has been widely explored using speech signals, which has shown significant improvement using deep models. Recently, there has been a surge in exploring faces and voices as they can offer more complementary and comprehensive information than relying only on a single modality of speech signals.

arxiv-2402-10022.title: Reproducing, Extending, and Analyzing Naming Experiments Note: This research was supported by the ISRAEL SCIENCE FOUNDATION (grant no. 832/18).
arxiv-2402-10022.creator: Rachel Alpern, Ido Lazer, Issar Tzachor, Hanit Hakim, Sapir Weissbuch, Dror G. Feitelson
arxiv-2402-10022.description: Abstract Naming is very important in software development, as names are often the only vehicle of meaning about what the code is intended to do. A recent study on how developers choose names collected the names given by different developers for the same objects.

arxiv-2411-08889.title: Multilingual Standalone Trustworthy Voice-Based Social Network for Disaster Situations
arxiv-2411-08889.creator: 1 st Majid Behravan, 2 nd Elham Mohammadrezaei, 3 nd Mohamed Azab, 4 th Denis Gračanin
arxiv-2411-08889.description: Abstract In disaster scenarios, effective communication is crucial, yet language barriers often hinder timely and accurate information dissemination, exacerbating vulnerabilities and complicating response efforts. This paper presents a novel, multilingual, voice-based social network specifically designed to address these challenges. The proposed system integrates advanced artificial intelligence (AI) with blockchain technology to enable secure, asynchronous voice communication across multiple languages.

arxiv-2412-12870.title: Physically Interpretable World Models via Weakly Supervised Representation Learning
arxiv-2412-12870.creator: Zhenjiang Mao, Mrinall Eashaan Umasudhan, Ivan Ruchkin
arxiv-2412-12870.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhenjiang Mao, Mrinall Eashaan Umasudhan, Ivan Ruchkin. Learning predictive models from high-dimensional sensory observations is fundamental for cyber-physical systems, yet the latent representations learned by standard world models lack physical interpretability. This limits their reliability, generalizability, and applicability to safety-critical tasks. We introduce Physically Interpretable World Models (PIWM), a framework that aligns latent representations with real-world physical quantities and constrains their evolution through partially known physical dynamics.

arxiv-2506-04945.title: Learning Joint Interventional Effects from Single-Variable Interventions in Additive Models
arxiv-2506-04945.creator: Armin Kekić, Sergio Hernan Garrido Mejia, Bernhard Schölkopf
arxiv-2506-04945.description: Abstract Estimating causal effects of joint interventions on multiple variables is crucial in many domains, but obtaining data from such simultaneous interventions can be challenging. Our study explores how to learn joint interventional effects using only observational data and single-variable interventions.

arxiv-2509-25644.title: Using Images from a Video Game to Improve the Detection of Truck Axles
arxiv-2509-25644.creator: Leandro Arab Marcomini, Andre Luiz Cunha
arxiv-2509-25644.description: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) traditionally require large amounts of data to train models with good performance. However, data collection is an expensive process, both in time and resources. Generated synthetic images are a good alternative, with video games producing realistic 3D models.

pmc-11674652.title: Histopathological Analysis of Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Liver Inflammation and Thrombus Formation in Mice: The Protective Effects of Aspirin
pmc-11674652.creator: Hayate Saitoh, Miina Sakaguchi, Fumito Miruno, Naoto Muramatsu, Nozomi Ito, Kanako Tadokoro, Kiyoharu Kawakami, Kazuhiko Nakadate
pmc-11674652.description: Hepatitis, a significant medical concern owing to its potential to cause acute and chronic liver disease, necessitates early intervention. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the histopathological features of lipopolysaccharide-induced hepatitis in mice, focusing on tissue alterations. The results demonstrated that hepatocytes exhibited decreased eosin staining, indicating cellular shrinkage, whereas sinusoids were swollen with blood cells.

pmc-11675040.title: Transcutaneous Spinal Stimulation Combined with Locomotor Training Improves Functional Outcomes in a Child with Cerebral Palsy: A Case Study
pmc-11675040.creator: Darryn Atkinson, Kristen Barta, Fabian Bizama, Hazel Anderson, Sheila Brose, Dimitry G Sayenko
pmc-11675040.description: Background and Purpose: activities-based locomotor training (AB-LT) is a restorative therapeutic approach to the treatment of movement deficits in people with non-progressive neurological conditions, including cerebral palsy (CP). Transcutaneous spinal stimulation (TSS) is an emerging tool in the rehabilitation of individuals with sensorimotor deficits caused by neurological dysfunction.

pmc-12472930.title: Human Gut Microbiota Profiles Related to Mediterranean and West African Diets and Association with Blastocystis Subtypes
pmc-12472930.creator: Lorenzo Antonetti, Federica Berrilli, Marina Cardellini, Massimo Federici, Rossella D’Alfonso
pmc-12472930.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: The effects of geographical origin, alongside age, diet, and drug treatments, on the gut microbiota have not been thoroughly analyzed in African countries. Furthermore, eukaryotic components, including Blastocystis, the most common intestinal protozoan worldwide, require further investigation. This study compares the gut microbiota of Italian subjects with that of two African groups to examine the influence of dietary patterns and the effects of Blastocystis presence and subtypes.
